title: Your Rights in the UAE: Work, Home & Money
tagline: Plain-English UAE law for everyday life: job contracts, gratuity, renting, consumer rights, online behaviour and resolving disputes.

superpower.name: Rights Aware
superpower.description: Knows the rules of daily life: avoids fines, scams and bad deals.

syllabus: Week 1: Working in the UAE: contracts, hours, leave and gratuity
Week 2: Renting a home: Ejari, rent rises and eviction rules
Week 3: Consumer rights, payments and staying safe online
Week 4: Resolving disputes and staying on the right side of the law

weeks.title: Working in the UAE
weeks.objective: Know what the labour law gives you, and what it expects from you.

slides.title: Your Employment Contract
slides.body: Private-sector work is governed by the UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021), overseen by MOHRE, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. All contracts are now fixed-term (they can be renewed), and they must be in writing.
bullets: Probation: up to 6 months
Notice period: as agreed in the contract, between 30 and 90 days
Salary paid through the Wage Protection System (WPS), on time
Your employer can't keep your passport
slides.takeaway: Read your contract before signing: it's the rulebook for your job.

slides.title: Hours, Leave and End-of-Service
slides.body: The law sets maximum hours and minimum leave, and rewards long service with a gratuity.
bullets: Normal hours: 8 a day, 48 a week; overtime paid at least 25% extra (50% between 10pm and 4am)
Annual leave: 30 days a year after a full year (2 days a month after 6 months)
Gratuity: 21 days' basic pay per year for the first 5 years, 30 days per year after that, capped at 2 years' pay
Public holidays are paid
slides.example:
Gratuity for 3 years on a basic salary of AED 6,000 a month:
Daily rate: 6,000 ÷ 30 = AED 200
21 days × 3 years = 63 days
63 × 200 = AED 12,600
slides.takeaway: Know your hours, your leave and your gratuity: they're your rights.

lab.title: Contract Check Lab
lab.brief: Read a sample job offer and list the probation, notice, hours, leave and how gratuity would be calculated.
lab.deliverable: A one-page summary of the contract terms.
lab.proTip: Ask for everything in writing: verbal promises are hard to prove.

options.explanation: Copies are fine; the original stays with you.

weeks.title: Renting a Home
weeks.objective: Rent with confidence: Ejari, deposits, rent increases and your protections.

slides.title: Ejari and the Tenancy Contract
slides.body: In Dubai, every residential lease must be registered on Ejari, the system run by RERA under the Dubai Land Department. Ejari makes the contract official: you need it for DEWA, residence visas for family, and any dispute.
bullets: Register the tenancy on Ejari
Security deposit: commonly 5% (unfurnished) or 10% (furnished) of the yearly rent
Agency fee: commonly 5% of the yearly rent
Keep receipts and photos of the condition on move-in
slides.takeaway: If it's not on Ejari, it's hard to defend.

slides.title: Rent Increases and Eviction
slides.body: Dubai's rent rules protect tenants from sudden changes. Rent rises at renewal are limited by the RERA Rental Index, and changes need advance notice.
bullets: Either side must give 90 days' notice before the contract ends to change its terms
Rent rises are capped by how far below the RERA Rental Index average you pay (0% to 20%)
Eviction to sell or for the landlord's own use needs 12 months' notice, sent through a notary public or registered mail
Disputes go to the Rental Dispute Centre
slides.takeaway: Check the RERA Rental Index before agreeing to any increase.

lab.title: Lease Review Lab
lab.brief: Review a sample Dubai lease: deposit, notice, maintenance responsibilities, and what the RERA calculator allows at renewal.
lab.deliverable: A checklist of the key terms and the maximum legal increase.
lab.proTip: Photograph every room on move-in day: it protects your deposit when you leave.

options.text: You must pay or leave in 30 days.
options.explanation: Changes need 90 days' notice, and increases are capped by the Rental Index.

options.text: Changes need 90 days' notice, and increases are capped by the RERA calculator; you can challenge it at the Rental Dispute Centre.
options.explanation: Notice periods and caps protect you.
Stopping rent puts you in breach.

slides.title: Your Rights as a Consumer
slides.body: UAE consumer protection law gives shoppers rights: accurate prices, honest descriptions, receipts and warranties honoured. In Dubai, complaints go to DET's consumer protection team.
bullets: Prices must be clearly displayed, in AED
You're entitled to a receipt in Arabic or English
Faulty goods: repair, replacement or refund under warranty
Shops must show their return policy
slides.takeaway: Keep receipts and complain through official channels: they work.

slides.title: Payments, Debt and Behaving Online
slides.body: Money and social media both come with rules. Bounced cheques and unpaid debts have serious consequences, and the UAE's cybercrime law covers what you post.
bullets: A bounced cheque is mostly a civil matter now, but cheque fraud is still a crime, and debts can still lead to bans
Credit history is tracked by the Al Etihad Credit Bureau (AECB)
Never post photos of people without consent, insult people online, or spread false news: these are offences
Report scams to the police (e-Crime platform) and your bank immediately
slides.takeaway: Online, assume everything you post is public and permanent.

lab.title: Rights in Action Lab

lab.proTip: Be specific: what you bought, when, what's wrong, and what you want.

weeks.title: Resolving Disputes
weeks.objective: Solve problems through the right channel, calmly and on record.

slides.title: The Right Door for Each Problem
slides.body: Most disputes have a dedicated authority that's faster and cheaper than court.
bullets: Work disputes: MOHRE (complaints, mediation), then the labour court
Rent: the Rental Dispute Centre (RDC)
Shops and services: DET consumer protection
Crimes, fraud and scams: Dubai Police (999 in an emergency, the e-Crime platform online)
slides.takeaway: Choose the right authority and you save months.

slides.title: Evidence and Calm
slides.body: Disputes are won with documents, not anger. Keep everything in writing and stay respectful: insults, even in messages, can become offences themselves.
bullets: Keep contracts, receipts, emails and screenshots
Write a timeline of what happened
Stay polite in every message
Ask for help: legal aid and community services exist
slides.takeaway: A calm person with a folder of evidence usually wins.

lab.title: Dispute Plan Lab
lab.brief: Pick a problem (unpaid salary, deposit not returned, faulty product) and write the step-by-step plan: evidence, authority, deadline.
lab.proTip: Start with a polite written request: many problems end there.

options.text: Send a polite written request with your evidence, then file at the Rental Dispute Centre if they still refuse.
options.explanation: Documented request first, then the right authority.

options.text: Change the locks on the flat.
options.explanation: You've moved out; that's not a remedy.
